title: The Story of Bread
summary: Bread is one of the oldest foods in the world. How did people first make it, and why is it still so important?
paragraphs: Bread is eaten every day by millions of people around the world. It comes in many shapes and sizes: long French bread, round flat bread from Central Asia, soft white bread and dark heavy bread from Germany. But where did this simple food come from?

Scientists believe that people were making a kind of bread more than fourteen thousand years ago, even before they started farming. They collected wild grains, broke them into small pieces with stones and mixed them with water. Then they cooked the mixture on hot stones next to a fire. This early bread was flat and hard, but it gave people energy and could be carried on long journeys.

When people began to grow wheat and other grains about ten thousand years ago, bread became even more important. Farmers could produce large amounts of grain and store it for the winter. In many places, bread became the main food of ordinary families.

The ancient Egyptians are often given credit for an important discovery. They noticed that if a mixture of flour and water was left in a warm place, it started to grow bigger. This happened because of yeast, a tiny living thing in the air. When this mixture was baked, the bread was soft and light. Egyptian workers who built the pyramids were sometimes paid with bread and beer.

In many cultures, bread is more than just food. It is a sign of friendship and respect. In some countries, guests are welcomed with bread and salt. In Central Asia, bread is never thrown on the floor, because people believe this shows a lack of respect. Families often share a large round loaf at the start of a meal.

Today, most bread is made in big factories by machines. This makes it cheap and easy to buy. However, in recent years, more and more people have started baking bread at home again. They say it is relaxing, and they enjoy the smell of fresh bread filling the kitchen. After fourteen thousand years, bread is still part of our lives, and it probably always will be.

questions.question: How did the first people make bread?
options: They baked it in large ovens
They cooked broken wild grains mixed with water on hot stones
questions.explanation: People broke wild grains into small pieces, mixed them with water and cooked them on hot stones.

questions.question: Why did bread become more important when farming began?
options: Farmers could produce and store large amounts of grain
questions.explanation: Farmers could grow large amounts of grain and store it for the winter.

questions.question: What made Egyptian bread soft and light?
questions.explanation: Yeast made the mixture grow, so the baked bread was soft and light.

questions.question: According to the text, what do people in Central Asia avoid doing?
questions.explanation: Bread is never thrown on the floor, because this shows a lack of respect.

questions.question: Why are more people baking bread at home now?
options: They find it relaxing and enjoy the smell
questions.explanation: The text says people find home baking relaxing and enjoy the smell of fresh bread.

grammar.explanation: We use the passive when the action is more important than the person who does it.
grammar.example: Today, most bread is made in big factories by machines.

exercise.question: Choose the passive sentence.
options: Most bread is made by machines.
Most bread is making by machines.
exercise.explanation: Passive = is/are + past participle: is made.
